"Defending is easier: defense counts x1.25 in a village and x1.5 in a castle (capital). In the open field (on a road) there is no bonus."
"The 'effective defense' values in the report ALREADY include the location bonus. Use them directly; do not apply the bonus again."

"Counter triangle (a BONUS, not an automatic win): spearman counters knight; archer counters spearman; knight counters archer. Having the counter multiplies your force by 1.5. The MOST NUMEROUS type of each army sets the counter matchup (ties in count break in the order spearman, archer, knight)."

So if the attacker's most numerous is knight, and defender's most numerous is spearman, then spearman counters knight. That means the defender has the counter (since their spearman count the attacker's knight). So the defender gets the 1.5 multiplier to their force. The attacker does not get a multiplier because their knight is countered, not countering. So the defender's effective defense is multiplied by 1.5. Their effective defense is 13, so becomes 19.5. "The side with the HIGHER effective force wins."
Let's look at how effective force is calculated.
Usually:
Attack force = sum of attack values of all troops, multiplied by 1.5 if the attacker's most numerous counters the defender's most numerous.
Defense force = sum of defense values of all troops, multiplied by 1.5 if the defender's most numerous counters the attacker's most numerous, and then multiplied by 1.25 (village) or 1.5 (castle).

Let's review the JSON format:
{
  "build": [ {"villageId": <id>, "type": <"spearman" | "archer" | "knight">, "quantity": <n>} ],
  "movements": [ {"fromId": <id>, "toId": <id>, "troops": {"spearman": <n>, "archer": <n>, "knight": <n>}} ],
  "plan": "<note>",
  "statement": "<text>"
}

It doesn't say "only the attacker gets it" or "only the defender gets it". It says "Having the counter multiplies your force by 1.5." So if your army's most numerous type counters the opponent's most numerous type, you get the bonus.

If attacker is archer, defender is spearman: attacker's type (archer) counters defender's type (spearman). So attacker gets the bonus.
If attacker is spearman, defender is knight: attacker's type (spearman) counters defender's type (knight). So attacker gets the bonus.
If attacker is spearman, defender is archer: defender's type (archer) counters attacker's type (spearman). So defender gets the bonus.
So the side that has the "counters" relationship gets the bonus.
